checks: Report validates against /task/output_schema.json (217 results; the round-1 'confidence' error is repaired, last entry confidence='low').

Re-derived the dchi2 decomposition from out/q40r2/analysis_N_H.txt by subtracting the cold (Tk<=30) and hot (Tk>=100) per-datum terms. X=40: 24.21-6.97=17.2 (prior 3.77-0.69=3.1, HCO+ 12C 11.0-4.4=6.6, CS 4.75-0.50=4.3, HCN 1.08-0.03=1.0, 13C 3.61-1.35=2.3). X=63: 17.39-13.18=4.2 with the prior term 9.31 in both branches, 13C 2.71-0.97=1.7. These match the summary and the report. I agree. The decomposition shows the discrimination is mostly carried by the 12C HCO+ and CS lines plus the band-scale/eta prior, with only about 2 of 17 coming from the 13C lines. This is stated candidly in the summary, but the report headline still reads as a '13C result'.

The ratio-only test (13C 3-2/1-0 = 0.277+-0.06) gives dchi2=0 between branches at every Tk. That is physically sensible, since a free (n, N13) can reproduce one ratio at any Tk, so the 13C data act only through the tie N(H13CO+)=N(HCO+)/X. I agree with this reading and with the withdrawal of the round-1 'excluded at >=4 sigma' and 'hot 170-300 K' wording.

The conclusion depends on X: dchi2 is 17 at X=40, 4 at X=63 and about 0 at X>=80. The data prefer X_N~31-35 (10/15% scales) or 40-51 (looser), which is at the low end of the Tang+19 range. The X prior is partly circular, because the data choose the X that favours the hot branch. The worker flags this (the conclusion needs X<~60). Treat the Bayes factors (15-1200) as model-conditional. The span across prior widths is the honest number: 'moderate to strong, one-zone, X<~60'.
Tk is only bounded from below (>~50 K), because the best solution sits at the 300 K grid cap. The worker states this and does not claim a hot temperature. I agree.

N(HCN)/N(HCO+) = 3.5-3.85 at N and 2.2 at S, N/S = 1.6-1.8, with P(N/S>1)~0.98 at about 2 sigma profile significance. This is stable against the branch and consistent with the team-a forum posts p0041/p0042. They find N core T poorly constrained, P(Tc_N>=Tc_S)=0.41, and a hot envelope allowed but not required. Our 'Tk>~50 K' and their 'hot allowed, not required' are not in conflict. Their Tc is the core temperature in a two-zone model, ours is a one-zone effective Tk. Say this explicitly.

The per-datum print-out labels 'band offsets ln' with values of -1.2 to -3.5. These cannot be ln scale factors with a 10% prior (chi2 would be hundreds), so they are presumably grid-index or sigma units. This is a labelling issue in s236, not a numerical error, because the quoted prior terms (0.3-13) are sensible. I did not edit the worker's files.

Aperture/beam: the primary result uses only the Harada 1.7 arcsec 12C+13C set, so the beam is matched by construction. The H13CN 1-0 / 2.2 arcsec variant carries an extra 30% systematic and gives the same N answer. I accept this.

fixes.how_experts_do_it: State the posterior probability together with its prior conditions (X prior, band-scale prior, one-zone) and the data terms that drive it. Do not quote a Bayes factor without them.

H13CN 4-3 is in Xb47 spw20 at the 4.2x2.8 arcsec beam, and the earlier Q4 limit (p0007, HCN/H13CN > 8.3 at the N core) was not fed into the RADEX fit. Then run that follow-up: take the Xb47 HCN 4-3/H13CN 4-3 ratio (same cube and beam, so beam-matched) or its limit as an extra constraint, N(H13CN)=N(HCN)/X, with the same X nuisance.
fixes.why: The item asked for H13CN, and the optically thick HCN branch is exactly what H13CN would test. The worker used H13CO+ and a 2.2 arcsec H13CN 1-0 instead, which is an acceptable substitute but not what was asked.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Use a same-cube, same-beam ratio of line to isotopologue as an opacity constraint, and include non-detections as censored likelihoods in the fit.
